items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: That was my favorite drummer. He was left-handed. That's why I guess I take him to him, because I was left-handed. Uh-huh. And he taught me and showed me.

How old were you when you started out?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: See, he played with that band and played with Ory's band at that time, and I knew of him, you know, see.

ctx.x: I just remember who was playing with him. I don't know who had the band, did you hear? No, I don't remember all that.

Now Pete could tell you, yeah, he could tell you just who was playing out there. But he used to lay off from there on Sunday night, Saturday, Sunday, or Monday night, and play with Ory. See, he played with that band and played with Ory's band at that time, and I knew of him, you know, see. That was around 1917, 1918. Frankie Dewson played out there a good while, and I don't know whether he was playing with Frankie Dewson or not. See, he could have been. Frankie played with the manager of the band out there.
It must have been the Eagle or something.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Henry Martin was the first one I seen do it.

ctx.x: And you took the cymbal out?

Yeah, take the cymbal beat off, you see. Throw it off, you see. They were both together, you know. It's genius. And it would be a sound nice. Henry Martin was the first one I seen do it. Mm-hmm. And it sounded real nice. But the guys now, they want to scarf their rims. They got pretty drums now, you know, see. And they wouldn't want to do that, because it would make all white marks on your drum. It would be because the drum was stained dark oak. Just like the children's snare drums is now in the parade. Well,…
Well, when did the guitar solos start? Did they always have that when you started? I imagine they were. They were playing them way back with the Columbia band? Way back with the guitar. Yeah.
